21.title: FTP Bounce Attack
21.result:
1.) Configure a FTP Public Server using the firewall Public Server Wizard on the LAN of the firewall, with a public address of the WAN IP Address of the firewall. Make sure that the FTP Server allows anonymous login.
  2.) Using Nmap configure the command line with nmap -vv -b anonymous:anon@[WAN IP Address of the firewall] [LAN IP Address of the FTP Server, or any other LAN IP Address).
  3.) Send the scan to the firewall.
  4.) Verify the log displays a message that the packets were dropped and contains the correct information for FTP: PORT bounce attack dropped.
  5.) Verify that an initial connection is established through FTP, but no further traffic is passed and the FTP bounce attack will time out after three tries.

7.steps:
Either nmap, or nemesis can be used to send the packets. In the case of nemesis there is only one packet being sent and this may not be enough traffic to set off the port scan feature of the firewall. When using nemesis you may have to repeatedly send the same packet 3-6 times before you see the appropriate message.
  For nemesis type nemesis tcp -v -f[flag] -D[WAN IP Address] The following flags can be used: E = NULL Stealth Scan C = NULL Stealth Scan F = FIN Stealth Scan FPU = XMAS Stealth Scan
  For nmap type nmap -vv -s[flag] [WAN IP Address] The following flags can be used: N = NULL Stealth Scan F = FIN Stealth Scan X = XMAS Stealth Scan

6.title: Firewall will reply with RST to Invalid TCP Packets while NOT in STEALTH Mode
6.result:
1.) In the Firewall - Advanced Rule Options page, disable Stealth Mode.
  2.) On the remote computer, enable a packet trace utility such as Ethereal, or EtherPeek and set it to capture all traffic from the firewall in both directions.
  3.) From a remote computer, send an invalid TCP recieved out-of-state packet. Use the Nemesis tool from the command line and type nemesis tcp -v -fSA -D[WAN IP Address] This will send a SYN-ACK without first sending a SYN.

20.steps:
There are two important requirements associated with the idle (zombie) station:
  The unsuspecting zombie station must be idle (thus the name "idlescan"). The idlescan needs an idle zombie workstation to ensure that the IP identification frames will remain consistent throughout the duration of the scan. The zombie station must provide consistent and predictable IP identification (IPID) values. If the operating system of the zombie does not provide predictable IPIDs, nmap will provide an warning before the scan begins: WARNING: Idlescan has erroneously detected phantom ports -- is the proxy 192.168.0.7 (192.168.0.7) really idle? If the scan cannot complete because of too many inconsistencies, nmap provides a final error message: Idlescan is unable to obtain meaningful results from proxy 192.168.0.7 (192.168.0.7). I'm sorry it didn't work out. QUITTING!
